claims.text: The alloy under study is an Fe-Cr-Co-Ni-Mo high-entropy alloy.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the alloy's oxide layer.
High configurational entropy reduces the driving force for oxide grain growth.
High configurational entropy promotes formation of a dense protective oxide scale.
A dense, stabilized oxide scale improves oxidation resistance.
The relevant structural mediator is a continuous, adherent Cr2O3-rich oxide layer.
Pre-oxidation treatment will improve the oxidation resistance of the HEA relative to the untreated HEA.
The pre-oxidized HEA will have a thinner oxide layer than the untreated HEA after oxidation testing.
The pre-oxidized HEA will show less mass gain than the untreated HEA after oxidation testing.
The proposed comparison is isothermal oxidation in air at 800 degrees Celsius for 100 hours, with pre-oxidized and untreated specimens.
Configurational entropy alone may be insufficient to produce the desired oxidation resistance.
Impurities or defects may dominate the oxidation behavior.

contradictions.description: The proposed governing variable is configurational entropy, but the controlled comparison changes pre-oxidation treatment while using the same HEA in both groups. Thus, the experiment does not directly manipulate or control configurational entropy and cannot isolate its causal role.
